title: Three Days and One Short Bowl
subtitle: 饮食与营养 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）
meta: 主题语境：饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）　|　核心词汇：snack　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 snack 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1966 the cook ① shared the snack that no guest in the canteen would have counted, and he said the sharing was the whole of the day. The ② snack, meaning the bite itself and not the bowl, ran three days and stayed uncounted in the book; a snack, he said, is the only thing in a canteen that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ snack in that canteen had the same short bowl beside it, and the ④ snack at the far table, meaning the portion they kept for the children to share and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A snack, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the cook said the counting is the part that fills three days.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the snack was the whole of the matter, meaning the pleasure and not the bite. The ⑥ snack, meaning the pleasure and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; snack, he said, is either something you share or the only word that means both a bite and a pleasure. He said the pleasure is the part they remember.

By 1971 the ⑦ snack had become a line in a menu, and the menu had become an argument about the short bowl. The ⑧ snack of the whole thing, the cook wrote in September, was one canteen and three days of counting; snack, he said, is either the portion at the far table or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ snack I remember is the bite counted in the menu, which closed in 1973 and is still counted as the quietest in the canteen. A ⑩ snack, my mother said in 1975, is the only bite that improves by being counted; every snack, she said, is a pleasure that has agreed to look like a bite. She said the pleasure was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 小吃；零食（指食堂里每一份旁边的那一份）
B. n. 小吃；零食（指那份小吃本身，与小小的碗相对）
C. 固定搭配：share the snack 分这一份小吃
D. n. 小吃；零食（指留给孩子们分着吃的那一份）
E. n. 小吃之事（抽象总称，指一处食堂的小吃之事）
F. n. 小吃；零食（指菜单里写到、被清点的那一份）
G. n. 小吃、小乐（指一件事里人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 小乐（抽象总称，指人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: shared the snack that no guest in the canteen would have counted

the snack at the far table

answers.why: share the snack 意为“分这一份小吃”，1966 年那位厨子把食堂里没有一位客人肯清点的一份小吃做了一遍。
snack 意为“小吃；零食”，指那份小吃本身而不是小小的碗，它经过了三个日子而在簿子上没有被清点。
snack 意为“小吃；零食”，指食堂里每一份旁边的那一份，每一份旁边都有同一只小小的碗。
snack 意为“小吃；零食”，指最远那张桌角的留给孩子们分着吃的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
snack 意为“小吃、小乐”，指一件事里人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份小乐就是那件事的全部。
snack 意为“小乐”，指人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西而不是那份小吃，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
snack 意为“小吃；零食”，指菜单里写到、被清点的那一份，到 1971 年这一份成了菜单里的一行。
snack 意为“小吃之事”，厨子九月写道，整件事的小吃之事是一处食堂和三个日子的清点。
snack 意为“小吃；零食”，我记得的是菜单里清点过的那一份，1973 年开完了，至今仍被说成食堂里最安静的一份。
snack 为抽象总称，母亲 1975 年说，小吃是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的小吃。
